title: TurboTab v2 crosswalk: what the engine surfaces, by quest-log stage
how_built: Seven stage maps (one per ruled stage, read-only over the repo at 2627066d) were merged.
Items with the same id, or the same engine decision under different ids, were folded into one; every folded map item is listed in merged_from and cross_refs.
Each item lives in exactly one stage: the stage where the user decides it. A noticing shown earlier carries noticed_at; later appearances are returns_at.
All 367 catalog threads are covered: either as their own thread: item, or inside the engine item that already represents them (threads field).
Containers (Models' noticing cards, Results' context-line groups, First look's Settled lines) are in groups, not items.
Patched the same day after the completeness critic's review (29 gaps): each gap verified against the source first; those not taken are listed at the end of CROSSWALK.md.

schema.id: Stable id: q: (a Router question), decision:, default:, noticing:, reading:, refusal:, preview:, exhibit:, result:, flowchart:, export:, gate:, other:, record:; thread:<catalog id> for a noticing from the understanding catalogs. sentinel:<family code> for a family sentinel (UNDERSTANDING_LAYER §3.3, U10).
schema.stage: The ONE quest-log stage the item lives in (data, question, first_look, whos_in, models, results, writeup).
schema.order: Position within its stage: the recommended order of the Decide objectives first, then Confirm, For the record and Shown.
schema.kind: question, decision, default, noticing, preview, refusal, exhibit, result, flowchart, export, other.
schema.title_plain: The card-facing title in plain words.
schema.engine_source: file:symbol references (several, separated by ;). Catalog threads cite docs/turbotab-next/understanding/catalogs/<lens>.json:<thread id>.
schema.objective: Decide, Confirm, For the record, or Shown (not an objective).
schema.goals: describe, inference (Estimate an effect), prediction (Predict), or all.
schema.lenses: dietary, clinical, metabolomics, genomics, survey, other, or all.
schema.tapestry: What the canvas shows (Focus, Strip, Flow, Routing, Angles; FOUNDATION §5).
schema.card: For a noticing: the card or question it is decided on.
schema.threads: The catalog thread ids this item represents.
schema.noticed_at: The earliest stage that shows it before its home stage (for example First look).
schema.returns_at: Later stages where it returns (a context line, a refusal exit, a sentence).
schema.merged_from: Every stage-map item folded into this one, as 'stage|id'.
schema.cross_refs: The other stage maps' view of the same item, with their objective and notes.
schema.placement_reason: For a catalog thread: why it lives in this stage.
schema.first_look_group: For a noticing shown in First look: its group (Who is in the data, What is missing, Each variable, Variables together, Over time and by batch, The outcome).
schema.exhibit: For an exhibit, including the four flowcharts made before training: pre_included, placement_default, placement_allowed, why, and drafted wordings by claim strength.
schema.family: For a catalog thread: its family (UNDERSTANDING_LAYER §3.1; Appendix A, or for the 34 threads the completeness review added, the family its failure_prevented text names; family_source says so).
schema.families: For an item carrying catalog threads: the families of those threads.

stages.name: 1 · Your data
boundary_issues: **The roles answer is refused in Your data.** QUESTION_KEYS puts 'roles' after target, event, task, follow_up, purpose, grain, repeat_kind, unit, aggregation and temporal (interview.py:QUESTION_KEYS). sequence.py:_answers_in_order refuses set_roles with 'not_yet' while any of those is open. The ruled order puts 'what each column is' in stage 1 and those questions in stages 2 and 4. Only the non-Router readings (confirm_reading(s), confirm_role, set_column_unit, set_categorical) can be recorded here.

**The engine asks readings where they are used, not at upload.** ask.py places the ask card on the consumer's question ('shown where the first consumer needs it, not as a wall at upload'). CONSUMERS are aggregation, survey and exclusions (Who's in), and estimand, adjustment, energy_adjustment and models (Models). BLUEPRINT §14.2 rule 1 says to ask only where it matters. §14.3 says the consumer sets a question's scope (code_question), so asking codes or amounts in Your data would ask about columns no consumer reads. UNDERSTANDING_LAYER §2.1 says the same: 'asked is not asked at First look'. This conflicts with the ruled scope 'what each column is: units, codes, identifiers, kinds'.

**First look depends on Your data in a way the engine does not provide.** FIRST_LOOK_BRIEF §1.1 says First look comes 'after Data' and reads only settled readings (units, roles, the energy column, sample roles). The engine settles most of those in Who's in or Models. So either Your data must settle them (against point 3), or First look must draw unsettled readings as proposals.

**A reading confirmed on a future outcome is orphaned.** confirm_reading and confirm_role refuse the outcome column (decisions.py:_reading_names_a_column, target_has_role). A reading confirmed in Your data on a column later chosen as the outcome is left behind. The outcome's own unit, kind, scale and order are Your question's (set_outcome_unit, set_task, set_outcome_scale, set_outcome_order).

**Joins happen before the table is turned.** Joins run at ingest, before orientation (build_graph: ingest, then oriented). A sample sheet keyed by sample ID cannot be joined to a genes-in-rows matrix, whose sample IDs are column names until it is turned (thread genomics-sample-sheet-alignment). PLAUSIBLE, not run.

**A join after the roles answer may drop new columns silently.** The roles answer stays answered (the Router never re-asks it), and model_predictors reads settled roles only (models/pipeline.py:model_predictors). Columns a later join adds get no role and are silently left out of the predictors. PLAUSIBLE, not run.

**set_feature_table is not sealed.** The oriented stage reads it, but it is in neither seal.py:DECISION_A nor DRAW_READS. Changing the annotation columns after the seal could change which columns become samples (rows). PLAUSIBLE, not run.

**The omics scale finding mixes a reading with a modeling choice.** The omics_scale finding (methods/omics.py) offers normalization methods (log_cpm_tmm, log_cpm, qc_pqn_log2) as a pre-seal repair, beside the reading 'declared_normalized'. MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 4 places the omics chain in domain transforms (Models).

**Reference rows and QC-RLSC straddle two stages.** They sit in the 'repairs' slot, before the seal and on reference rows only, which makes them an assay-pack item in Your data. But the QC rows leaving is a participant-flow step (Who's in; working 7/8, cohort 6). Their placement needs a ruling.

**The design hints point to a question no stage has yet.** The outcome-prevalence hint needs set_target (Your question). The arm, matched-set and case-control hints point to a design question the engine lacks. The ruled 'second question picks the shape' sits in Your question, so the hints recorded here have no consumer until the designed-experiments milestone.

**Unit questions are asked in Who's in.** The energy unit and day count, body-measure units and sex coding are asked today by the screens' refusal or the ask card at exclusions. The ruled scope places units in Your data.

**The engine asks for a tap the threads want silent.** SAS transport zeros are 'silent: repaired silently' per the thread, but the engine requires apply_repair. Under the ruling that open noticings must be decided before the seal, this makes a trivial item a Decide.

**The survey reading and question are split across stages.** The survey design columns (role:design) are read here. The survey question that consumes them is asked only under inference (_survey_gate), after purpose (Your question) and the roles. Under prediction the same columns feed design-based CV with no question.
gaps: **No seven-stage map in the engine.** The Router knows only QUESTION_KEYS. Only lens and orientation of the stage's Router keys fall in Your data. Many of the stage's elements have no stage, no objective label and no progress count: join_files, import_codebook, confirm_reading(s), confirm_role, set_column_unit, set_categorical, set_feature_table, apply_repair, defer_finding, dismiss_finding and every finding. A stage registry has to own: when Your data is done, what counts toward the bar, and the 'reopened because…' reason.

**No Confirm-sweep composer.** readings.read_from_data and GET /projects/{pid}/readings exist, but nothing builds a per-stage list of defaults with number-changing alternatives. No component calls useReadings (frontend_inventory).

**No For-the-record source.** No endpoint collects the ingest warnings (DatasetInfo.warnings, the XPT member notes), the profile basis, not-applicable reasons and checked-clean detectors. The 'checked clean' state of the understanding layer's thread lifecycle is not built.

**No data-in UI.** The frontend has client functions for files, join-preview and codebooks, but no component calls them, so join_files and import_codebook have no path from the UI (frontend_inventory, gap 'assembly (DATAIN)').

**Controls never emitted.** set_feature_table and set_categorical are never emitted. confirm_role and set_column_unit arrive only through refusal or ask-card exits. So the 'what each column is' readings cannot be answered in Your data from today's UI.
**No sheet or member picker.** Only the first Excel sheet and the first XPT member are read, so those warnings cannot become a Decide.
**Stacking files with a shared schema (NHANES cycles) is not built.** The DoD amendment of 2026-10-05 approved it, and HANDOFF.md lists it as approved and not yet built.
**No practice datasets on the Start screen.** The DoD amendment of 2026-10-05 folds Classic's practice datasets into the demo; StartScreen.tsx has no demo entry.

**No design-hint store or detectors.** A randomized-arm reading, matched-set detection, a case-control prevalence reading, cluster randomization and the design question itself all belong to the designed-experiments milestone. Next's GrainAnswer has no matched-set answer; legacy turbotab/grain.py's DESIGN_NOT_DESCRIBED was not carried over.

**The thread registry (UNDERSTANDING_LAYER.md) is not built.** No noticing has an open, dismissed or left-open state, an 'Affects …' first-feed stage, or a consumed-by log. No general gate requires open noticings to be decided before the lock or seal: plan_lock.py reads no findings, and seal.py gates only findings on the draw's columns.
**No QC-RSD figure.** Only qc_rows.parquet is written beside the working table, so the QC-RLSC decision has no Angles view.

**No consolidated per-column ledger view.** The roles artifact gives the proposals and /readings gives the settled readings, but no endpoint lists every column with every reading kind (role, unit, days, codes, sex, nesting): its state (settled by the values, by the codebook, by the user, or open) and the consumer that needs it. Without one, Your data cannot show 'what each column is' as a single canvas.

**No reopen reason.** The Router never reopens an answered later question; it marks stages stale (interview.py docstring). The ruled 'a reopened stage drops back and says why' needs an engine reason, such as 'the join added 12 columns, so the roles are re-read'.

stages.name: 2 · Your question
stages.order_notes:
Recommended order within the stage:

1. **The outcome** (q:target), with its picture: the rows that record it, and its distribution.
2. **The outcome card's rows,** in the engine's routing order: the event, the kind (with its scale or order follow-up and the unit), and the follow-up and its window.
   - interview.py QUESTION_KEYS asks them as target, event, task, follow_up.
   - sequence.py OUTCOME_QUESTIONS lets event, task and follow_up be answered in any order among themselves.
   - The outcome-definition noticings sit here too (diagnosed or diseased, defined from columns, ascertainment, consequences of the outcome, zeros, counts, bounds, competing death). They are asked where their first consumer needs them, and all must be decided or dismissed before the lock or the seal.
3. **The design** (new), before the goal: it changes which goals and wordings are valid. A case-control sample allows no prevalence; a trial makes adjustment precision-only.
4. **The goal** (q:goal), worded around the outcome. The engine already places it after the outcome: _answers_in_order refuses the purpose 'not yet' while event, task or follow-up is open.
5. **The shape,** filtered by lens and task: the Describe shapes, the Estimate shape, and for Predict the intended use and moment of use. The metabolomics study-question card goes here.
6. **'Add another goal'** (tracks).
7. **The Confirm sweep, last.** It covers:
   - a yes/no outcome counted over one period when nothing reads as follow-up;
   - the prediction horizon at the median follow-up;
   - observational as the design.

   A Confirm flip can create a new Decide (for example, 'follow-up varies' makes the outcome a time to event, which then needs its time column), so the sweep must reopen the list.
8. **For the record,** collapsed and not counted toward progress:
   - a task settled by values;
   - the not-applicable steps;
   - the original scale and numeric order;
   - the sentences, checklist anchors and plan slots.

The stage has no results or exhibits of its own. Its previews feed the Who's in flowchart: the 'outcome recorded' step, and a landmark's rows.
boundary_issues: Your data's 'what each column is' depends on this stage. The roles stage reads target, purpose, task, follow_up and outcome_scale (stages/__init__.py roles reads); proposals reads target, purpose, task and event; interview.py asks 'roles' after grain, unit, aggregation and temporal, which are Who's in. The roles therefore cannot be settled in stage 1 before the outcome and goal exist: either move the roles question after Your question, or reopen Your data when the outcome or goal is set. The same applies to threads whose consumer is the roles: outcome proxies, items downstream of the outcome, and the moment of use.

The outcome's reading depends on Who's in. target_info depends on working, and working reads grain, unit and aggregation. An aggregation answer re-reads the outcome (its task, its follow-up candidates). The 'which outcome to keep' choice (first, last or mean; sequence.py:_aggregation_knows_the_outcome) defines the outcome but is asked in Who's in, and it is constrained by the task. clin-state-or-event needs settled time points, also a Who's in answer.

The target preview (fact_previews.target_views) and scale_question's evidence (skew, median, max) read the outcome on every row before the seal, and are not recorded as outcome views. FIRST_LOOK_BRIEF §6.1 says that under prediction an outcome-alone (O1) view comes after the split, on training rows, and is recorded. So for a Predict goal, or a shared First look under the strictest rule, Your question shows an outcome view that the brief's rule would hold back.

First look sits before the seal (stage 3) but the engine needs the seal first. stages/__init__.py declares explore requires=('target','split'), and LOCKBOX_CONSTITUTION §01 orders lens, repairs, target, grain, eligibility, SEAL, EDA, with nothing resequenced. Under a Predict goal, First look's outcome group cannot open before Who's in draws the seal. The goal is chosen here, so this is where the conflict is triggered.

The engine's purpose has two values (decisions.py Purpose), and Describe is not one of them. About 159 two-valued purpose branches, plus fallbacks to 'prediction' in contracts.py:ContractOption.for_purpose, custom_sound.py and methods/missing.py, would route a third value as prediction. Usual intake, a Describe shape, is gated to inference today (usual_intake.py), and the survey-population question, central to Describe, is not applicable under prediction and asked only under inference, in Who's in.

Sequential tracks against a single-valued state. ProjectState holds one target and one purpose. A seal and an opening belong to one outcome (decisions.py:_for_this_outcome), and changing the target after a holdout is refused until a re-seal. Tracks need per-track outcome, goal and seal slots, or a project per track.

Track order against the plan lock. server/service.py:_lock_after_prediction locks an inference plan at once, as 'declared after estimates were seen', if any estimate was shown under prediction. An Estimate track must therefore be declared and locked before a Predict track's Fit, or run first.

A shared Who's in conflicts with purpose-scoped rules. Under prediction, multiple imputation is refused; under inference, single fill and indicators are blocked and recorded (decisions.py:_missing_fits_the_purpose). The seal is also purpose-scoped (BLUEPRINT §12 ruling 3). Missing values and the split cannot be one shared answer across Estimate and Predict tracks, and inference reading the prediction holdout's outcomes could leak into the Predict track.

Describe shapes with no outcome (patterns, clustering, Bland-Altman between methods, usual intake) conflict with 'the outcome, then the goal', and cohort, seal_plan and explore require target. Who's in's participant flow cannot be computed without an outcome.

The shape question overlaps the Models estimand. Exposure family or single exposure, substitution, and time-varying are asked in Models after the split (estimand, time_varying). Intended use is placed at MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 2, lives as an Explore lever (stages/explore.py:_use_lever), and its preview needs a fit. A shape answered in stage 2 has no slot, and would have to pre-fill or route those later questions.

The design question's stage is unruled. Its threads point to 'the design card' and the metabolomics 'study-question card'. It changes valid goals and wording, so it must come before the goal; it could equally be placed in Your data.
The event: thread shared-which-level-is-the-event proposes the event from vocabulary, but the core never guesses it (EventAsk: 'Never guessed (OPENING_SEQUENCE §03.2)').

Changes after results. The ruling says an inference change after the lock becomes a secondary analysis; the engine instead marks later decisions after_estimates and replaces the plan in force (decisions.py:disclose), with no secondary path for a new outcome or goal. For prediction, the ruling keeps the earlier version; the engine refuses target or task changes after the holdout until a re-seal, and 'shared-step changes after scores kept as versions' is deferred to v2.x (DoD §5).

A follow-up landmark, answered in Your question, removes rows from the Who's in participant flow (cohort reads follow_up; follow_up_views draws 'Rows at risk at the landmark'). The shelf's Riley event count ignores the horizon (INBOX 243), so a horizon change does not recompute it.

The energy-related-outcome finding computes the outcome's correlation with energy, an O3 view, in the findings stage as soon as the target is set, before the goal is known. The thread says this must be held until the lock under inference.
gaps: Engine: a third goal, Describe, routed through every purpose branch, contract label, checklist (STROBE descriptive) and sentence (voice._PURPOSE_CLAUSE).

Engine: the Describe shapes. Survey-weighted means and prevalence by group (no descriptive design-based estimator), trends across stacked cycles (stacking not built), Table 1, dietary patterns, clustering, and Bland-Altman agreement. Usual intake exists but is gated to inference and has no Router key.
Engine: a shape slot and question filtered by lens and task, and a design slot (observational, trial, case-control, matched sets) with 'Not available yet' exits that keep the work.
Engine: per-track state (a goal per track, possibly a subject per track), a track order rule, and a checklist and manuscript merge across tracks.

Engine: the outcome_definition reading (diagnosed or disease, cut-point from columns, ascertainment), competing events, interval censoring, the moment-of-use and deployment question, and the target population.
Engine: outcome tasks for counts with an offset, zero-mass (two-part), and bounded (beta, fractional logit, Tobit) outcomes; smearing retransformation for a log outcome under prediction.
Engine: method contracts for the outcome scale, order and unit, and for the follow-up (landmark, horizon, censoring), which METHODS_REFERENCE lists as gaps.
Previews: the event draws only a note; the goal draws only a note (it needs a Routing view of what each goal brings); intended use needs a fit; the follow-up landmark Flow is unreachable.

Frontend: TaskAsk lacks the ordinal and time-to-event options and the evidence (fits, histogram, skew numbers, unit). No control exists for set_outcome_unit, set_intended_use, or the follow-up's landmark, horizon, entry and prediction horizon. target_info.follow_up_options is unread and undeclared in schemas.

Frontend: the quest-log presentation of this stage is unbuilt: Decide, Confirm and For the record grouping, the Confirm sweep, the collapsed record list, and the seven-segment progress bar with drop-back. The calm-quest prototype shows the outcome and purpose only as stated sentences (fixture 'stated' target and purpose), not as questions.
Understanding layer: no thread contract, registry, context line or 'worth a look' exists yet, so the outcome-card and follow-up-card noticings have no host.

stages.name: 3 · First look
stages.order_notes:
First look sits after Your question and before Who's in. Its objectives come in this order.

(1) Arrival is read-only. The index shows every column in column order, with the outcome hidden. 'Worth a look' shows at most three highlights, ranked by tier, then reach, share, excess and column order. Nothing is asked until an item is opened.

(2) Decide, T1 first. A blocker replaces the primary action with 'Decide this first', because nothing downstream is valid until it is answered. Examples: a batch perfectly confounded with the outcome; a run that cannot be QC-corrected as exported; a table the wrong way round.

(3) Decide, T2, through the first-visit walk: 'Look at the first' → 'Next · 2 of 3' → 'Continue to Who's in'. Each item either opens 'Decide now' (only where the routed question's NEEDS are met) or is carried forward as an open noticing reading 'Comes up at Who's in / Models'. It resurfaces there attributed, and must be decided or dismissed before the lock or the seal.

(4) The six groups, in the fixed STRATOS order: Who is in the data → What is missing → Each variable → Variables together → Over time and by batch. They can be browsed at will. The order never changes, so a map learned in one lens carries to the others.

(5) The outcome door comes last, and its rule depends on the goal:
- Predict: opens only after the split, on training rows.
- Estimate an effect: a counted door, never on the default path, never ranked.
- Describe: no rule yet.
- Several goals: the strictest goal's rule governs.
It comes last because O1/O3 views are the forking-path risk. Outcome-free looks may shape the plan; outcome looks may not.

(6) Confirm: normally empty here. First look owns no number-changing default that has an alternative. The rows a look reads and the references beside each measure are For the record. A thread item labeled Confirm is a default owned by its consumer, so it is swept at Who's in or Models.

(7) For the record:
- readings settled at Your data or Your question, shown as 'Settled' lines;
- checked-clean lines per group;
- the rows-read basis;
- view_outcome records and Explore's methods sentence.

How the thread items are labeled:
- engine_source is docs/turbotab-next/understanding/catalogs/<file>#<id>.
- objective comes from the thread's tier: asked or surfaced → Decide; stated → Confirm; silent → For the record; O3 → Shown.
- notes give the view class and the quest stages its feeds return at. O0 is outcome-free, O1 the outcome alone, O2 outcome × design, O3 outcome × predictor.
- goals come from each consumer's per-purpose text. 'describe' was added by rule for outcome-free data-fact threads, because the engine has no Describe purpose.
- status:
  - partial: the detector exists and surfaces today as a finding card or a Router question, but not as a First look look;
  - built-engine-only: it exists only in stages the frontend never fetches (explore, calibration…);
  - missing: new;
  - new-scope: designed-experiment and dietary-pattern threads.
- Every thread reopens the same way. A data-changing decision re-measures it ('Changed since you looked'). A settled thread whose numbers move past its tolerance is asked again.

Counts: 241 threads are noticed here and 64 are listed as settled earlier. 41 are noticed on a later card and 21 are born late; both lists are under boundary_issues. Together these cover all 367 catalog ids.
boundary_issues: Under inference the brief opens the outcome door from the start. The engine cannot: it reads 'every analyzed row' from the cohort (the exclusions and missing-values answers) and from the split. Both are Who's in decisions, and the split is asked under inference too (seal.py). Either the door waits for Who's in under both goals, or a new scope reads the oriented rows before eligibility.

Who's in redefines the table First look measured. The working stage reads grain, unit and aggregation; roles, target_info, proposals, cohort and every other reader of the working table depend on it. First look therefore runs on the oriented, unaggregated rows. A grain or aggregation answer rebuilds the working table and re-measures the looks: recall rows become persons, and First look reopens. Threads that need settled repeats can show only their structure until then: diet-day-to-day-variance, diet-few-replicate-persons, diet-zero-is-a-day, shared-unit-repeats and others.

Roles conflict. Looks need settled roles: for reach, for context variables, for the sex and energy columns. But the roles question is QUESTION_KEYS #13, after grain, repeat_kind, unit, aggregation and temporal. The roles stage also reads the working table, the target and the purpose. The ruled stage 1 puts 'what each column is' before the outcome. That conflicts with the engine for stage 1, and leaves First look with proposed (unsettled) roles unless roles settle earlier.

The rank key's reach ('touches the exposure', brief §3.2) needs the declared exposure. The ruled order declares it in Models (estimand, QUESTION_KEYS #19). Use the exposure role proposed at Your data; otherwise rank without it.

interview.route opens only the first unanswered question, and every later one waits on it. 'Decide now' into exclusions, missing values or the energy model (Who's in, Models) is therefore out of order. It needs a Router exception: the question's NEEDS are fresh, and no earlier question it depends on is open.

Repairs need a placement rule. The current Record shows findings with repair options before the outcome question (Record.tsx RepairsSection) and the rest below as 'noticed'. That split is a rendering rule (repairs.length > 0), not a stage rule. Value meaning (K1) belongs to Your data. But two repair options feed the participant flow (Who's in): impossible values' 'exclude rows', and the QC rows leaving after drift correction.

The findings stage reads the target, for the batch × outcome verdict and the energy-related-outcome dispute. Changing the outcome in Your question after First look recomputes the findings and reopens First look.

Survey under prediction conflicts. Explore's survey_design finding offers set_survey under prediction, but interview._survey_gate makes the survey question not_applicable under prediction (INBOX:230).

Explore's levers belong to other stages: set_levers, set_selection and set_exposure_form to Models, and set_intended_use to prediction's Your question. First look should only link to them. None has a Router key.

'Before the lock or the seal' is ambiguous under prediction. UNDERSTANDING_LAYER §7 Q1 is ruled as 'before the seal opens' (open_seal, the last step), and §2.6 says before the held-out rows are scored. If 'the seal' meant drawing it at Who's in, every First look noticing would have to be cleared one stage later.

Progress accounting is undefined for noticings surfaced in First look but decided at Who's in or Models. Proposed here: First look's segment counts highlights opened and T1 items decided; a carried noticing counts in the stage that decides it.

Thread placement is derived, not declared. The catalogs carry no first_at moment and no First look group, so group, view class and placement here come from looks_at, the detector text and the consumers, then hand-corrected. These 41 need a later declaration (the exposure, the adjustment set, a model or the seal) and are noticed on their own card, not in First look: diet-substitution-support, diet-invisible-exposure, diet-healthy-lifestyle-cluster, diet-quantiles-sort-by-sex-and-size, diet-deployment-measurement-heterogeneity, diet-ratio-features-share-the-outcome, diet-meaningful-increment, clin-confounding-by-indication, clin-time-zero, clin-incremental-value, clin-treatment-during-follow-up, clin-biomarker-on-the-path, clin-contraindication-positivity, metab-correction-honest-check, metab-normalizer-carries-biology, metab-detectable-effect, metab-cross-batch-transport, metab-wide-noise-ceiling, genomics-new-site-new-platform, genomics-genotype-shapes-the-diet, genomics-polygenic-score-provenance, genomics-allele-harmonization, survey-reliability-attenuation, survey-small-sample-psychometrics, survey-instrument-published-scoring, survey-item-overlap-with-outcome, shared-exposure-varies-between-groups, shared-mediator-or-confounder, shared-time-varying-feedback, shared-interaction-support, shared-exposure-family, shared-positivity-overlap, shared-treatment-paradox, shared-time-zero, shared-missing-confounder, shared-score-fitted-on-these-rows, shared-holdout-too-small, shared-mismeasured-confounder, shared-many-versions-of-the-exposure, shared-sensitive-attribute-role, shared-identifiable-values-in-the-export.

These 21 threads are born late: they need a fit, so they never enter First look and belong to Results: diet-borrowed-validity-coefficients, clin-expected-directions, metab-enrichment-background, metab-treatment-marker, metab-panel-instability, genomics-signature-instability, genomics-pvalue-distribution, genomics-enrichment-background, shared-score-within-noise, survey-common-method, survey-estimate-reliability, survey-explanations-describe-the-sample, shared-model-no-better-than-baseline, shared-selection-unstable, shared-primary-model-diagnostics, shared-overfit-calibration-slope, shared-decisions-after-viewing, shared-winner-optimism, shared-rashomon-disagreement, shared-learned-interaction, shared-null-is-inconclusive.

Dietary patterns and clustering (new v2 methods) need to stay apart from First look's display-only PCA, which is the embedding view. A declared pattern is an exposure in Models (the diet-patterns thread), with k set by a declared rule.

Two owner questions from FIRST_LOOK_BRIEF §9 are not recorded as ruled in HANDOFF.md: Q1, the outcome door under inference (a door, or hidden until the lock); and Q3, the 'embedding' and 'matrix' view kinds. Q2, the walk on the first visit, reads as ruled: 'walked on the first visit'.

Neither the prototype nor the foundation matches the ruled structure yet. calm-quest's sections are the STROBE methods heads (Participants, Variables, Data sources and measurement, Statistical methods, Results), not the seven ruled stages. FOUNDATION §3/§6 still describe the Q&A card.
gaps: A pre-seal 'notices' stage (UNDERSTANDING_LAYER §5 U4) is missing. It would hold each look's measure, reference, reach and rank key, the rows each view class reads, and a cache per data state. Today turbotab/core/stages/findings.py:findings_stage sorts by severity, confidence and id, and Explore's outcome-free checks run only after the seal.

No thread is wired end to end; about one in five has engine pieces. Missing: the thread registry and contract (U1); the ledger extension (U2: subject shapes, meaning kinds, 'does not apply' as a value); the census tests (U3).
Findings and threads have no six-group key, and no group has checked-clean records ('27 columns: no reading beyond its reference'). finding.group is only a pager key.
The quest log has no First look entry. There is no QUESTION_KEY for it. The walk, mastery and the progress-segment rule are not built, and the calm-quest prototype has no First look section.
'Decide now' cannot open a later question out of order in interview.route. A deferral can target only a QUESTION_KEY (repairs.py:_deferral_has_a_place), not a card-family row or the outcome door.

The outcome door's UI is missing: a control that posts view_outcome; an ExploreFinding → ConsequenceView adapter; labeled classes; a searchable 'With one column…' list in plan order; views for categorical predictors and for multiclass, ordinal and time-to-event outcomes. Outcome points must not ship in the artifact before a view is opened.
The index is not seal-aware. profile_stage, /columns and /columns/{name}/histogram read every row, the outcome included.

View vocabulary gaps: 'embedding' is reserved but not built, and 'matrix' needs a design decision. Footprint layouts and Angles have no engine field (PreviewResult, MethodContract), and the context view and hexbins are missing. purposes.py:VIEW_PURPOSES needs 'data_ok' entries for looks.
Approved v2 views that are not built: Classic's missingness patterns, skew and outlier table and pre-fit VIF table (V2_DEFINITION_OF_DONE amendment 2026-10-05), and Table 1.
The looked-at ledger, the IDA paragraph, supplement S1 with the clean-check list, and 'Add to the supplement' on Save are all missing.

Dismissal is partial. Noticed finding cards (those with no repair) have no dismiss. The thread form of dismissal (confirm 'not_applicable', with its sentence) and the cleared list of open noticings before the lock or seal (U8) are missing.

Seven Explore lever options route nowhere (decision None): scale, measure, adjustment twice, missing, by-hand variance and by-hand collinear. Explore also ignores the lens: 'lens' is in EXPLORE_READS but never read.

Describe and sequential tracks are missing. decisions.Purpose is prediction or inference, ProjectState holds one purpose, and ViewOutcome.rows is one value. The shared First look's strictest-goal rule needs state for several tracks.
Heavy compute needs scheduling and caching: per-feature passes, permutation chance shares and PCA. Nothing may run on hover, and long CPU runs need asking first.

stages.name: 4 · Who's in
stages.order_notes:
Engine order inside the stage: the Router asks grain, repeat_kind, unit, aggregation, temporal, [roles], clusters, survey, exclusions, missing, split, in that order (turbotab/core/interview.py:QUESTION_KEYS). It refuses any answer the Router has not reached yet with 'not_yet' (turbotab/core/sequence.py:_answers_in_order). Roles fall inside this run but the ruling puts them in Stage 1; see boundary_issues.

Proposed order of objectives for the quest-log stage:

(1) DECIDE, in Router order, in four blocks:
- What is one row: grain, then repeats or time points, then unit, then combining, then predicting forward. The combining question needs the outcome (sequence.py:_aggregation_knows_the_outcome), which is why this block cannot open before Stage 2.
- Who groups: clusters, then survey. The clusters question needs the roles; the survey question needs the proposals stage and the goal.
- Eligibility: exclusions. The screens' own reading asks sit on its ask card (ask.py:CONSUMERS 'exclusions'), and noticings routed to it resurface here (interview.py:with_deferred).
- Missing values, with their deferred noticings.

(2) UNDER PREDICTION, two more Decide items close the stage:
- The open-noticings gate for the draw. Findings that would rewrite the outcome, the unit id or the time column must be settled first (seal.py:_the_draw_reads_settled_values, interview.py NEEDS split: findings). This follows the rule that noticings are decided before the seal.
- The seal itself.

(3) CONFIRM: one sweep of the number-changing defaults. Under prediction it cannot come last. The draw reads the stated repeat kind, the temporal time column and the stated grain, and changing these after the seal is refused (seal.py:DECISION_A, _the_draw_holds_until_a_reseal). So the sweep runs before the seal, and the seal is the stage's final Decide. Under inference and Describe, the sweep comes last as ruled.

(4) THE PARTICIPANT FLOWCHART (samples and features for omics) closes the stage. It is drawn after the seal so its last box splits development from held out (turbotab/core/export/figures.py:participant_flow).

(5) FOR THE RECORD, collapsed. This holds the stated grain, the outcome-measured, reference-row and landmark steps, the every-row analysis, survey domains, the stated validation methods and the split under inference.

Why this order: structure feeds working, which feeds roles and target_info (stages/__init__.py). Proposals feed the survey and exclusions questions. The cohort feeds the split, and the seal plan reads the clusters and grain answers.

A possible reorder: the draw reads only the outcome, the unit id and the time column, never the exclusions or the missing-values answer (seal.py:draw_columns; rows.py:draw_split). So the prediction seal could follow the row block directly. That would let First look's outcome group open sooner, but only if _answers_in_order is relaxed for set_split.
boundary_issues: Roles (Stage 1) sit after the row block in the engine. QUESTION_KEYS asks grain, repeat_kind, unit, aggregation and temporal before roles, and sequence.py:_answers_in_order refuses set_roles until those are answered or skipped. The roles stage reads 'grain' and the working table that unit and aggregation reshape (stages/__init__.py roles reads grain; deps working). On repeated-measures data, Stage 1 cannot finish before Stage 4's row block. Options: move grain, repeats and unit into Your data, or let roles be answered first and re-confirmed after the reshape.

Combining is downstream of the outcome and upstream of its reading. It refuses without the outcome (sequence.py:_aggregation_knows_the_outcome 'no_target'). target_info reads the working table it rewrites (stages/__init__.py target_info deps working), so the task, event and follow-up of Stage 2 are re-read after Who's in. Findings also read 'aggregation', so First look's checks recompute.

First look comes before the seal, but the engine's exploration needs it. The explore stage requires target and split, depends on cohort, and reads missing and split (stages/__init__.py explore). MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 row 1 puts Explore after the seal, and FIRST_LOOK_BRIEF §1.1 opens the outcome group only once the split is recorded. The engine refuses set_split until exclusions and missing are answered, so under prediction First look's outcome group waits for Stage 4.

FIRST_LOOK_BRIEF §7.1 assumes the survey question was answered at Data ('Settled, because the survey question was answered at Data'). The ruling puts survey in Who's in, after First look, so the 'Who is in the data' group would show it unsettled.

Survey under prediction has no home. The Router marks it not_applicable (survey.py:not_applicable_reason), yet set_survey is accepted under prediction (survey.py:_asked_under_inference, ruling 13) and drives design-based CV, which explore and evaluation offer in First look and Models.

Clusters under inference decides a model term: fixed effects plus CR2 (estimand.py:grouping_card). The design and fit read it, and shared-exposure-varies-between-groups feeds it from the selection stage. It is a Models decision asked in Who's in.

Missing values are asked in Who's in but depend on Models. MODELING_SEQUENCE row 6: asked before the seal, executed after the forms. Passive MI is blocked once a spline, quintiles or a logged energy model is declared (decisions.py:_imputation_fits_the_analysis; methods/missing.py:missing_block holds the fit). Complete cases read the predictors the adjustment answers keep (decisions.py:left_out uses estimand.adjustment_left_out). Models can therefore reopen Who's in.

The participant flow is not final at the end of Who's in. Steps come later from Stage 2 (the landmark: rows.py:landmark_of) and Models (the consumers-only domain: rows.py:domain_of reading form_domains; complete cases recounted after the adjustment set). Sensitivity analyses add row sets. The flowchart needs a provisional state, or a redraw at the analysis flowchart.
set_sensitivity has no Router key. The calm kit put it under Participants, but under inference it is a declared secondary that the plan lock covers, which points to Models.

Reference rows (pooled QCs) leave in the working table before the outcome is read (reference_rows.py:reference_filter). They must be settled before Stage 2's task reading, or 'QC' becomes a class. Only their flow step belongs in Who's in.

A Stage 4 answer can refuse a Stage 2 change: set_target while a rule reads the new outcome (decisions.py:_new_outcome_has_no_rule); set_follow_up while a rule reads its time column (_follow_up_has_no_rule); set_target, set_task, set_temporal or a draw-column repair after a holdout (seal.py:_the_draw_holds_until_a_reseal); set_purpose to inference over copies read as repeats (structural.py:_inference_over_copies_read_as_repeats). Reopening Stage 2 must drop the bar back through Who's in.

Decision A: orientation and join_files (Stage 1) and grain, unit and aggregation (Stage 4) are refused once the seal is drawn (seal.py:DECISION_A). Reopening Stage 1 after the seal first requires withdrawing it.

Which seal? The ruled 'noticings decided before the lock or the seal' and UNDERSTANDING_LAYER §7 ruling 1 (under prediction, before the seal opens, i.e. open_seal in Results) differ. The engine only requires draw-column findings to be settled before the draw (seal.py:_the_draw_reads_settled_values). A ruling is needed on drawing versus opening.

'Confirm last' collides with the seal. The stated repeat kind, the temporal time column and the stated grain are read by the draw, and changing them after the seal is refused. Under prediction the Confirm sweep must come before the seal Decide.

Sequential tracks share Who's in, but its answers are validated per purpose, and there is one ProjectState slot each (decisions.py:ProjectState). MI is refused under prediction ('imputation_with_the_outcome') while a single fill is block-and-record under inference. Exclusions rank in opposite orders. Clusters' 'adjust' is refused under prediction. Survey is not asked under prediction. The split leads differently. One shared answer cannot serve an inference track and a prediction track.

Under inference, the split and temporal questions change no reported number: no CV score is shown (ruling 13) and a holdout is labeled unsound. The Router still asks both (interview.py has no gate for split or temporal), so the ruled labels would make them For the record.
The missing question is routed even when no predictor has a blank (interview.py has no gate for it). It should then go to For the record.

Never overwrite silently: under inference, post-lock changes are only marked after_estimates (plan_lock.py; decisions.py:disclose), not converted into secondary analyses. Prediction's 'after_scores' holdout status and versions (RECIPES §3.3, F14) are specified but not built.
gaps: Zero-row refusal: nothing refuses when exclusions, complete cases or a domain leave 0 (or too few) rows. The design stage fails with scikit-learn's 'Found array with 0 sample(s)' (INBOX.md:255). A cohort-level refusal is needed that names the step, with exits: impute, drop the rule, leave the columns out.

Chronological draw: an unorderable time column raises ValueError in rows.py:split_stage, which surfaces as a stage failure. It needs a Refusal with exits: another column, mean combining, or a random draw labeled exploratory.
No Describe purpose: decisions.py:Purpose is prediction|inference, so the survey, missing, exclusions and split gates are undefined for Describe.
No tracks in the engine: one ProjectState, so the shared Who's in cannot hold per-purpose answers.

No design declaration: randomized, cluster-randomized, case-control and matched sets are absent. GrainAnswer lacks the legacy DESIGN_NOT_DESCRIBED hatch. There are no ITT or per-protocol analysis sets, no post-randomization exclusion refusal, no CONSORT flow, and no 'Not available yet' options.

The flowchart engine draws rows only (figures.py:participant_flow): no unit counts under a repeated grain, no ghosted survey domains, no leaver-vs-stayer comparison per step (shared-selection-flow), no omics samples-and-features flow (metab-feature-flow), and no provisional marking when Models adds steps.

There is no per-stage 'reopened because' signal. The Router keeps later answers 'answered' when an upstream answer changes (interview.py docstring); only refusals, stage staleness and the form's 'stale' follow-up exist.

There is no stated-default inventory for the Confirm sweep. The Router knows only asked, skipped and not_applicable. Number-changing defaults with alternatives (exclusion missing='exclude', Goldberg CVs, m, imputation model and levels, below-detection fill, split settings, weight choice) need an engine listing per stage.

The thread layer is not built (UNDERSTANDING_LAYER: about one thread in five has engine pieces). Noticings for this stage appear only as findings. There is no moment, context line or open-noticings gate before the seal (§2.6).
There is no pre-seal 'look' stage for First look's outcome-free checks (FIRST_LOOK_BRIEF §8). The explore stage's quality-by-group check needs the split.
Prediction cannot group folds by a non-unit cluster with more than 30 levels (shared-grouping-above-the-person).

Frontend gaps: the Record is a linear list with no stage grouping, no seven-segment bar, no Confirm sweep and no For the record list. Clusters reads only roles proposed as 'cluster', so structural groupings yield only 'No grouping'. SealAsk has no validation scheme, floor or labels. MissingAsk is hard-coded: no below-detection, no imputation model or levels, no m, no ranked labels. ExclusionsAsk records one rule, refused screens look pressable, and there is no by-level or 'keep unrecorded' option. RepeatKindAsk has no imputed copies or level order; AggregationAsk has no per-column rules; SurveyAsk has no design read. complete_case_loss is unread. set_sensitivity and reseal cannot be emitted, and there is no export UI for participant_flow.svg.
Post-lock conversion: an exclusion, missing, survey or cluster change after lock_plan is not turned into a declared secondary analysis.

stages.name: 5 · Models
stages.map_title: 5 · Models (inference: exposure and effect, adjustment set, time-varying lane, energy model, forms, modifiers, causal lane, model families, declared secondaries, plan lock; prediction: split/validation, intended use, selection and in-fold levers, model families, recipes, tuning, long-fit hold; Describe track's estimators; designed-experiments milestone; analysis flowchart and Fit; the Confirm sweep)
stages.order_notes:
Inside Models the objectives run Decide, then the open-noticings gate, then Confirm, then the flowchart and Fit. The Decide questions follow the engine's dependency order, because each card is computed from the answers before it. The ruled list differs from that order in places; the Router's order is used here.

**Inference track (QUESTION_KEYS):**
1. estimand
2. adjustment
3. time_varying: the Router asks it here, before the energy model.
4. energy_adjustment
5. form: its card is read on the exposure's final scale, after the domain transforms (MODELING_SEQUENCE §1 rows 4-5).
6. modification: stated; Confirm.
7. causal: stated; Confirm. causal_design needs estimand and adjustment.
8. models: the shelf counts the form terms.
9. Declarations with no Router key: Model 1 (set_model_sequence), multiplicity, sensitivity analyses, regression calibration, scales and batch. Each needs the estimand and the adjustment set. Calibration also records the adjustment set it was declared under.

**Prediction track:**
1. The split and validation scheme: the Router asks it right after missing values. See the boundary issues.
2. The energy model, dietary lens only.
3. The form, stated.
4. Intended use, then selection, then the in-fold levers.
5. Models, with Riley's minimum first.
6. Recipes, then tuning. Both are missing.

**Describe track:** usual intake and the Describe estimators.

**End of every track:**
1. One card lists the open noticings that feed the plan. The rule (2026-10-06) is that each must be decided or dismissed before the lock or the seal.
2. The Confirm sweep comes last among the objectives, by ruling, and only for defaults with an alternative that changes a number.
3. The analysis flowchart follows, with Fit. Under inference, pressing Fit is the first time an estimate is displayed, so it fires the engine's automatic plan lock. Under prediction, Fit carries the time estimate and the hold for fits over 2 minutes.

For the record items (intervals, quintiles beside the curve, withheld scores, benchmarks, the secondary model from the answers, the plan export) sit in the collapsed list and count toward nothing. Designed-experiment items replace the adjustment card when the design is randomized. The design question itself must come earlier; see the boundary issues.
boundary_issues: **The split and seal are placed twice.** The ruled list puts 'the seal under prediction' in Who's in and also 'the split and seal' in Models. The engine has one kind for both, `set_split` (the holdout draw plus the validation scheme), and the Router asks it after missing values, before the estimand. The shelf, design, fit and explore stages depend on the split, and First look's outcome views need it under prediction (explore requires split; FIRST_LOOK_BRIEF §1.1). So First look (stage 3) cannot open its outcome group until a stage-4/5 answer exists. Suggestion: draw the seal in Who's in and make the validation scheme a Models Confirm. That needs `set_split` split in two, or re-recorded.

**The Who's in participant flow depends on Models answers.** The cohort stage reads the adjustment answers: complete cases are counted on the covariates kept (WP17_READS). It also reads `form_domains`, so a consumers-only domain removes non-consumers on a line of their own, and the follow-up landmark. The flowchart at the end of Who's in therefore changes after Models. Who's in must reopen or mark the flowchart provisional.

**Missing values (Who's in) needs Models answers.** Multiple imputation compatible with the analysis model needs the declared forms, interactions and energy model, and 'a change of form or interactions invalidates the imputations' (MODELING_SEQUENCE §2). The Router asks missing before estimand and form.

**Column readings are asked in Models, not Your data.** The ask card sits on the estimand, adjustment, energy and models questions (`ask.CONSUMERS`). It confirms an exposure's role and whether each whole-valued predictor's numbers are codes or amounts. The ruled stage 1 is 'what each column is', but the engine places each reading at its first consumer by design (BLUEPRINT §14.2). The calm-kit puts these 'codes' steps under measurement.

**Substitution is always after the lock under inference.** The substitution question waits for a fresh fit (MUST_BE_FRESH) and its slot is in `plan_slots`, so it is recorded after the lock, as an after-estimates change. It belongs either beside the estimand's contrast before Fit, or the lock must exempt it.

**set_explain is part of the plan.** Under inference explain is an estimate stage, and the explain slot is in `plan_slots`. Requesting explanations in Results is therefore marked after the estimates were seen, and serving explain also locks the plan. respond_diagnostic and set_updating are inherently after the fit (Results), yet diagnostic_responses and updating are plan slots that reopen Models.

**The Router's order differs from the ruled Models list.** time_varying is asked right after adjustment, before the energy model and forms; causal comes after modification; models comes last. Under prediction the energy model (dietary) and the form (stated) also fall in Models, though the ruled prediction list omits them.

**Prediction choices are offered in First look.** Intended use, selection and the in-fold levers are offered as levers on First look's Explore findings (`stages/explore.py`). Their natural home is Models under prediction. `set_exposure_form` may be answered any time (ANSWERED_ANY_TIME), including from First look's relationship view. A lever set after an outcome view is disclosed as hand-chosen.

**Where is the exposure asked?** The exposure (estimand) sits in Models, but 'Your question' words the goal around the outcome. 'Estimate an effect' invites 'of what?' there (HANDOFF plain words: 'What do you think affects glucose?'). Exposure roles are also set in Your data.

**A user lock is refused.** The engine refuses a client-posted lock (service SYSTEM_KINDS, 'plan_locks_itself'). The calm-kit prototype's 'Lock the plan and fit the models?' step cannot be recorded; the lock must be the side effect of Fit's first estimate display.
**'Before the seal' is ambiguous.** For open noticings under prediction, UNDERSTANDING_LAYER §2.6 means before `open_seal` (Results). The ruled structure draws the seal in Who's in.

**Design must be declared before Models.** The design declaration (randomized, cluster, case-control, matched) must come before Who's in (no exclusion after randomization; ITT set; CONSORT flow) and before First look (no confounder search under randomization). The designed-experiments milestone cannot live only in Models.

**Direct effect vs mediation.** Mediation is out of v2, but the estimand still offers `effect='direct'`, with mediator–outcome confounder questions and an interaction attestation (`estimand.direct_questions`). Decide whether 'direct' stays, becomes 'Not available yet', or goes.

**Sensitivity analyses: Who's in or Models?** The calm-kit places the declared sensitivity analyses (`set_sensitivity`, alternative removal rules) under Participants; the ruled scope puts secondaries in Models. They read the exclusions (Who's in) and refit the chosen families (Models).

**Usual intake and the Describe track.** `set_usual_intake` runs under the lens and purpose, under either purpose; there is no Describe purpose. Ruled, it is the Describe track's Models, but today it would appear inside an inference or prediction run.

**Router order vs free navigation.** The Router refuses answers to questions still waiting behind earlier ones (sequence `_answers_in_order`). Free navigation in the quest log (hover the questions, jump ahead) must show later Models questions as waiting, not answerable.
gaps: **Fit must gate the fits and the lock.** There is no Fit command and no long-fit hold. The fit stage requires only `models`, so fits start as soon as `select_models` is recorded. The server locks the plan on the first estimate it serves (`service._lock_when_shown`), and Stage.tsx fetches the fit, so the lock is silent. The `served_gate` holds estimates only until follow_up, clusters, estimand, adjustment, time_varying and form are answered. Model 1, sensitivity, calibration, multiplicity, causal and modifiers can therefore become after-estimates changes. Needed: a Fit job command, or client gating of every estimate stage; and the 2-minute scheduler hold (RECIPES §4.4, RT-8).

**The prediction override machinery is not built:** `set_recipe`, `set_tuning`, `declare_version`, the stamps and versions (RT-1 to RT-8), the default that trees 'Try both' for blanks, nested tuning, and the four new families (ridge, Huber, random forest, XGBoost). `RECIPES_AND_TUNING.md` draft 3, which folds in Nolan's rulings, is not written.

**No engine list of stated defaults for the Confirm sweep.** Nothing returns, per stage, the defaults set for the user and whether an alternative changes a number. The Router reports only its skipped steps (causal, modification, form under prediction). The rest sits in contract ranks and completions.

**The understanding layer is unbuilt.** There is no thread registry, no claims or moments, no context lines, and no open-noticings gate before the lock or seal. About 300 catalog threads touch Models consumers, and about 1 in 5 has engine pieces.

**Ten Models decision kinds have no Router key and no UI path:** set_model_sequence, set_sensitivity, set_measurement_error, set_scales, set_batch, set_usual_intake, set_intended_use, set_selection, set_levers and set_explain. set_multiplicity is reachable only through the estimand's family answer. The quest log needs a routing rule for them, or the engine must add Router keys with gates (`METHODS_REFERENCE` marks batch and scales 'Asked: never').

**Six Router questions use GenericAsk** (estimand, adjustment, time_varying, form, modification, causal) and need bespoke cards. Their unread fields include measure labels, direct-effect questions, derived-role pills, knots and cuts, contrast levels, the second exposure's answers, trim, folds and repetitions, the lane's confounders and censoring, and overlap/ESS.
**Missing canvas views:** the overlap histogram with effective sample sizes, and the weights and positivity by time point. Neither is in the closed view vocabulary. Lineage role pills are not drawn.
**Engine preview defects (HANDOFF):** the energy preview quotes a coefficient before the lock, breaking FOUNDATION §5 rule 6. The exposure and estimand previews draw nothing.

**The analysis flowchart is not composed.** Its pieces exist: design lineage, the model-sequence story, per-family lineage and seal cells. Missing are one savable figure covering the crude model, Model 1/2/3, the secondaries and the causal lane (inference) or folds, families, recipes and tuning (prediction), and the Fit button placed on it.

**Post-lock changes are only disclosed.** The engine marks them after_estimates and refits the primary. The ruled behavior is that the locked primary stays and the change runs as a labeled secondary; today only modifiers (post hoc) and calibration behave that way.
**Prediction changes after scores are not versioned.** The 'revised after first results' earlier version is not built: scores-seen and openings are keyed by family (F14).

**No goal, track or design concepts.** Purpose is prediction or inference only, and ProjectState holds one estimand, one model set and one plan, so a Describe track and a second goal's Models cannot coexist. Design declaration and the trial, case-control and matched analyses are new scope.
**New v2 methods have no engine:** dietary patterns, clustering into subgroups, Bland–Altman, survey-weighted means and prevalence by group, trends across stacked cycles, and in-fold PCA for omics.
**Plan display is missing.** The analysis-plan export (GET /plan) and the after-estimates marks have no UI. The methods text has no UI either.

boundary_issues_resolved.resolved: Settled here: ruled, the gate is at the opening (UNDERSTANDING_LAYER §7 ruling 1).
Settled here: "Not available yet", with an exit to the total effect.
Settled here (Fit): the lock stays a system record, made when Fit is pressed; disagreement 12.

stages.name: 6 · Results
stages.order_notes:
Results is per track and begins only after the Fit press at the end of Models; under inference that press is also the lock. Placement never enters the Confirm sweep, because a placement changes no number.

INFERENCE (Estimate an effect):
1. The lock line is shown, not an objective: the time and the SHA-256.
2. Decide the primary exhibit's wording; its placement is fixed in Results. The primary is Table 2's primary and crude rows, or the declared marginal RD/RR, or the time-varying or causal estimate when that is the declared primary.
3. Decide a failed diagnostic's response (respond_diagnostic). It changes what sits beside the primary, so it comes before the companions.
4. Decide the declared companions in plan order, each pre-listed: Model 3 or the further-adjusted model, regression calibration, the scale correction, the causal lane, effect modification, the exposure-family table, the substitution curve.
5. Decide the sensitivity layer: the declared sensitivity analyses, unmeasured confounding (robustness value or E-value) and "Which of my decisions mattered?".
6. Decide the late-born noticings: diagnostic labels, inconclusive nulls, reversed directions, the p-value histogram. Any that asks for a new analysis becomes a secondary marked "after the estimates were seen".
7. Explanations come last. They are optional and heavy, and they describe the model, not the effect.
8. The Confirm sweep covers the explanation curve method and the substitution step and band.
9. For the record: the model-sequence display, the robustness-value-first order and the E-value SD, multiplicity, fit statistics withheld, and diagnostics that passed.

Why this order: the pre-included primary anchors every interpretation, and the methods floor (the primary is always reported; anything left out goes to the Supplement) applies only once it is worded. The companions and sensitivity analyses are read against it. Late noticings are labels and disclosures that attach to exhibits already on screen.

PREDICTION (Predict):
1. The cross-validated comparison and its declared-result basis: BBC-CV, the baseline and the spline benchmark. Their defaults are For the record.
2. Before the seal, Decide what MODELING_SEQUENCE row 12(a) requires to be fixed:
   - the final model (inside open_seal);
   - the decision threshold (Confirm) and model updating (set_updating);
   - the nested-CV offer when p > n;
   - every open noticing that changes the honest score (the ruled gate).
3. Decide open_seal, once.
4. The held-out result: pre-included, wording only.
5. Decide the remaining exhibits: calibration, the decision curve, subgroups, IECV, design-based CV, the interpretable model's cost, inclusion frequencies.
6. Late-born noticings: no better than the baseline, winner optimism, Rashomon disagreement, the calibration slope, the noise ceiling, the trust row.
7. Explanations. Serving them counts the floor scores as seen (selection.explained_in), so they follow the declaration.
8. Versions "revised after first results", inside the comparison only.
9. The Confirm sweep, then For the record.

DESCRIBE: the usual-intake distribution now, and Table 1, weighted prevalence and trends once built. Each is a Decide on wording and placement. There is no lock and no seal, and a Describe track locks nothing, so it can run before or after the others.

TRACKS: each track's Results follows its own Models. The lock is project-wide, and anything shown under prediction locks a later inference plan at once. So the inference track must come before a prediction track on the same project.
boundary_issues: The plan locks before the Fit press. service._lock_when_shown locks on the first served artifact of any estimand.ESTIMATE_STAGES stage, and the fit runs live unless it is expected to take over about 2 minutes (RECIPES ruling 2). So under inference the lock can happen before the ruled 'analysis flowchart where Fit is pressed'. The current frontend fetches the fit eagerly (Stage.tsx), so the lock already fires silently. The quest log must not serve any estimate stage until Fit, or the engine must hold inference fits for an explicit action. Open noticings must be cleared before that point, which falls in Models.

The substitution question lands in Results but feeds the plan. The Router asks 'substitution' only after the fit is fresh (interview.MUST_BE_FRESH). Under inference the pair and step are among plan_lock.plan_slots, since the substitution stage reads them, and the contrast (substitution or addition) is part of the estimand. So the pair is always recorded 'After the estimates were seen'. Under inference it should be declared in Models and only drawn in Results; under prediction it can stay in Results.

Post-lock changes conflict with the ruling. The ruled structure turns a post-lock change into a secondary analysis; the engine records it as after estimates and overwrites every estimate (decisions.disclose, plan_lock.plan_document keeps only the locked plan text). respond_diagnostic and post-hoc set_modification are post-lock by construction and already labeled (POST_HOC), so they fit the ruling. set_sensitivity, set_measurement_error, set_model_sequence and set_multiplicity declared late do not.

Prediction versions conflict with the scope cuts. 'Prediction keeps the earlier version, labeled revised after first results' needs RECIPES §3.2 versions, which are unbuilt. Shared-trunk changes after scores (the missing-values answer, the levers, the energy model, the forms) create no version: they were moved to INBOX v2.x by Nolan's 2026-10-06 ruling (V2_DEFINITION_OF_DONE §5). So for trunk changes, 'never overwrite silently' can only be met by disclosure in v2.

Sequential tracks do not fit one project state. The engine has one ProjectState with one purpose slot, one project-wide plan_locked, and a SHOWN_UNDER_PREDICTION file that is not keyed by track. A prediction track run first makes a later inference track lock immediately with seen='prediction' (service._lock_after_prediction). An inference track run first marks every later prediction-track decision 'After the estimates were seen' (decisions.disclose reads plan_locked). There is no track concept to keep each track's Models and Results apart.

Results decisions that rewrite earlier stages' slots, so the progress bar must drop back and say why: nested_offer records set_split (Who's in / Models); reseal reopens the split; genomics-pvalue-distribution and metab-treatment-marker reopen the batch, pairing, structure and routing questions; a regression calibration invalidated by an adjustment change is re-asked in Models.

Under prediction, open_seal sits in Results, but MODELING_SEQUENCE row 12(a) requires the threshold and recalibration fixed before opening. set_intended_use is placed at row 2 (Your question / Models), while its consequences (the decision curve, the in-fold threshold) and set_updating (shrinkage offered by the evaluation stage) only become visible after the fit. Both must be Decided in Results ahead of open_seal.

The engine's explore stage depends on split, so Explore runs after the seal (MODELING_SEQUENCE row 1), but the ruled First look (stage 3) comes before Who's in (stage 4, the seal). Results' hand-lever disclosure (evaluation.hand_levers) and the decisions-after-viewing thread read outcome views that, under prediction, can only be recorded after the seal.

Explanations are a Results item that changes earlier state. Explain is an ESTIMATE_STAGES stage: under inference serving it locks the plan, and under prediction it notes CV scores as seen (selection.explained_in), which keeps families in the compared set (_compared_families_stay). It cannot serve as a Models-stage preview, and it must follow the declaration.

Duplicate and conflicting exhibits. The secondary stage and Table 2's Model 3 fit the same 'further adjusted for' model. The scales stage shows a corrected coefficient for a score that Table 2 lists as an adjustment term, because a scale cannot be the estimand's exposure (INBOX 201, 295).

The export gate fires in Write-up, but its exits point into Results: 'Show the estimates; the first one shown locks the plan' and 'Declare X final and open the held-out rows' (gate.missing). Substitution is optional for export (OPTIONAL_QUESTIONS), and open_seal is treated as the open plan (PLAN_QUESTIONS).
gaps: No exhibit model in the engine. There is no decision kind for choosing a wording or a placement (Results, Discussion, Supplement, left out), no registry of 'every analysis run', and nothing enforces the methods floor: the locked primary and the held-out score fixed in Results, anything omitted sent to the Supplement and kept in the record.

No drafted result wordings and no claim-strength rule. The engine writes methods sentences (voice, effects.methods_sentence), single readings (effects.sensitivity_reading, interaction.sentence) and DeclaredResult.sentence, but no alternative wordings. Nothing separates association, effect-under-assumptions and prediction wording for observational designs: estimand.caption says 'The total effect of ...'.

Post-lock changes overwrite the primary. decisions.disclose marks the record and every estimate stage recomputes on the new state; no stage keeps the locked primary beside a labeled secondary, as the ruling requires. The calm prototype (walk.ts refitFor) does the same.

Prediction versions are unbuilt: set_recipe, set_tuning, declare_version, stamps, earlier versions as gray rows, the Settings table (RECIPES_AND_TUNING §3-4). Nested tuning for boosted trees, random forest and XGBoost is approved but not built.
'Which of my decisions mattered?' is not served by the engine; it is composed only in the explore/ prototypes.

Describe has no purpose value (decisions.Purpose is prediction or inference). Table 1, survey-weighted means and prevalence by group, and trends across stacked cycles are missing. Usual intake exists but has no Router key and no UI.
Bland–Altman, dietary patterns, clustering and the designed-experiment results (ITT and per-protocol, missing-outcome sensitivity, CONSORT) are missing.

Threads: no registry, notices stage, consumed-by log, context lines, trust row or supplement table S1 (UNDERSTANDING WP U1-U7). Most late-born O3/O4 detectors are new: the p-value histogram, the noise ceiling, Rashomon disagreement, ICE interactions, inconclusive nulls, treatment markers. The open-noticings gate before the seal (U8) is missing.

Missing consumers that Results threads feed: competing risks, IPCW, leave-one-batch-out and leave-one-site-out validation, process-only baselines, the deployment-noise re-score, the specification curve, weighted SHAP and ALE under the population answer, external validity coefficients, MNAR delta and quantitative bias analyses, and sensitivity analyses other than exclusion-rule row sets.

The closed view vocabulary (consequences.py: row_flow, lineage, distribution, relationship, table_focus) has no table, forest, curve, calibration, decision-curve, spec-curve, overlap or embedding kind. Exhibits need these, and each is a design decision.

Frontend: 11 result stages are never fetched (effects, sensitivity, secondary, calibration, scales, usual_intake, causal, explain, modification, explore, evaluation); the last three are not in AnyStageName. No control emits respond_diagnostic, set_explain, set_updating, set_sensitivity, set_intended_use, set_selection, reseal or lock_plan. The plan locks silently and after_estimates marks are not shown. Under inference, Coefficients.tsx shows the energy terms as if they were effects. There is no export UI.

Export: the bundle tabulates only Table 2 with its appendix and calibration, or the performance table (INBOX 250). Causal, time-varying, substitution, sensitivity, secondary, scales, usual-intake, explanation and evaluation results are not tabulated, and export/figures.py has no results figures. There is no LaTeX or Word export and no manuscript gate.

Contracts missing for Results methods (METHODS_REFERENCE 'Gaps'): substitution curves for one outcome, declared secondary and sensitivity analyses, calibration of continuous and binary predictions, DeLong, the price of explainability, the architecture lane, model updating, re-sealing. The multiplicity contract has no methods sentence.
